anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Optimizer inputs (row counts, histograms, correlation data) are stale or incomplete, leading the planner to choose systematically mis-costed execution plans.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly: Obsolete row versions and rollback records accumulate because background cleanup is throttled or blocked, inflating on-disk objects and visibility-check overhead.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The write-ahead log path (generation, flush, switch, archive, retention) becomes a bottleneck, stretching commit latency and stalling writers.

When these three root causes coincide, the system exhibits a multi-layer performance collapse:  
• Queries adopt inefficient plans—e.g., index probes where true cardinalities demand scans, or vice-versa—because statistics reflect the pre-bloat data shape rather than the current, heavily versioned heap.  
• Table and index bloat from unreclaimed versions drastically lengthens I/O paths; the mischosen plans amplify I/O and CPU consumption, further stressing the buffer pool and cache hierarchy.  
• Concurrently, surging redo from update/delete churn and from the faulty plans’ extra work overwhelms the log buffer and log device, inflating commit latency, causing frequent log-flush waits, and delaying checkpoints and archival.  
• Long-running transactions that keep version snapshots open also prevent log segment recycling, so log directories and version stores grow together, consuming space and triggering emergency autovacuum or checkpoint storms.  
• Background statistics jobs, vacuum/cleanup workers, and log archivers all contend for I/O and CPU, falling further behind and creating a feedback loop where stale statistics, bloat, and log pressure reinforce each other.  

Causally, excessive MVCC bloat inflates table sizes and redo generation, which in turn magnifies transaction-log throughput requirements. Log subsystem saturation slows commits and prolongs active snapshots, blocking vacuum from pruning dead tuples and perpetuating version accumulation. The expanding heap and skewed dead/live row ratios render existing statistics obsolete; suppressed or delayed statistics refreshes (due to long transactions or choking maintenance workers) lock the optimizer into poor plans that intensify CPU and I/O demand, generating even more undo/redo. This vicious cycle can escalate to severe space exhaustion, widespread query slowdowns, and potential outage if log or transaction-ID horizons are reached.

entry.official_description: Failed to update data directory flag for dd table with tablespace id '%llu' when ibd file for '%s' is moved to new location '%s' during server shutdown
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
